opportunities.gap: The MDX body and the misconceptions file contradict each other on the most load-bearing point of the section. The MDX consistently frames printed text as loading the VISUAL channel because it 'enters through the eyes' (lines 26, 62, 78, 88, and the step-reveal answerIndex). But the misconceptions file (cma_channels_are_modalities, feedback field) says printed text 'is processed in the VERBAL channel, the same route used for narration.' These are two different and mutually exclusive readings of Mayer's dual-channel model (the sensory-modality interpretation vs the presentation-mode interpretation). A learner who reads both will be confused about which channel printed text loads. Mayer's canonical treatment uses the sensory-modality interpretation for channel definition (eyes->visual/pictorial channel, ears->auditory/verbal channel), which is what the MDX uses; the misconception feedback as written is wrong and undercuts the entire section.
opportunities.proposed_change: Rewrite the cma_channels_are_modalities feedback to align with the MDX sensory-modality framing: 'Printed text enters through the eyes, so it loads the VISUAL channel alongside the picture/animation and the two compete for the same limited capacity. Route the explanation to spoken narration so the verbal stream travels through the idle AUDITORY channel.' Also rename/rewrite the description, which currently says channels are NOT defined by sense organ, the opposite of what the MDX teaches. Reconcile the 'pattern' label too.
